expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Long/receive CORRA_2027-03 (CRAH27): overnight CORRA 2.29% versus Mar-27 implied 3.13% (+84bp) and a 2028 peak near 3.65% (+136bp). The holding-period return is implied-minus-realized if that catch-up is not delivered.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Long USDCAD to collect the overnight differential (SOFR 3.85% versus CORRA 2.29%) as the FX carry analogue of an easier Canadian policy path versus a hiking Fed.
expression_comparison.rationale: Rates is the cleaner patient expression. The CORRA 2027-03 receive owns the overpriced BoC hike path directly and is paid if realized overnight stays nearer 2.29% than 3.13%. Long USDCAD is genuine USD-over-CAD carry, but the pair is already at the 87th percentile of its 5y distribution, energy-market shock absorbers and CAD energy beta can overwhelm FX carry, and AUDCAD is a 5y extreme so CAD-cross carry is exhausted. When both expressions are live, the seat prefers rates.

context_build.causal_mechanism: The trade tests whether Canada will be forced into the 84bp of tightening priced into CRAH27 by March 2027. Mechanism: energy keeps headline inflation at 3% and BoC minutes flag higher pass-through risk, but core stays near 2% and the labor gauge (38) and consumer gauge (45) say the tightening channel is already biting demand. If pass-through stays in the headline rather than becoming broad, realized CORRA stays far below 3.13% and a 2027 receiver earns the implied-minus-realized gap as the contract rolls toward overnight. That is carry, not a heroic easing call.
context_build.path_to_current_price: FACT: CORRA overnight is 2.29% as of 2026-09-17. One-month CORRA is still near overnight into October (2.305%) then lifts to 2.43% in November and 2.58% in December. Three-month CORRA then prices 2.775% by Dec-26, 3.13% by Mar-27, 3.365% by Jun-27, and 3.51-3.65% through 2027-28. Canadian 2Y sovereign yield is 3.27% (97.8th percentile of its 1y distribution) after +31bp over 1m, while CA-US 2Y is -140bp (3.8th percentile 1y). USDCAD is 1.401, up 1.74% over 1m, 74th percentile 1y and 87th percentile 5y. The path is a global tightening impulse (Fed hike to 3.75-4.00%, BoJ to 1.25%, hawkish BoE hold) leaking into Canadian term rates and CAD weakness even as Canadian overnight remains 2.29%.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: KNOWN: Canadian overnight is 2.29%; August headline inflation holds at 3% with core near 2%; energy-market shock absorbers have weakened; Fed was heavily priced for a 25bp hike and then delivered it; CA-US rate differentials were already historically wide. MARGINALLY NEW for this cutoff: the hike is now realized tightening (SOFR printed 3.85% on 2026-09-17, up from 3.62% on 2026-09-16), BoC minutes explicitly flag higher energy pass-through risk, BoJ and a hawkish BoE split broaden the global duration impulse, and a Saudi workaround modestly cuts the extreme oil-supply tail. The new information explains why CA term rates can stay bid without proving that Mar-27 CORRA should be 84bp above overnight.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: CRAH27 at 3.13% assumes about 84bp of Canadian tightening by the 2027-03 window, with the curve still climbing to roughly 3.51% by Sep-27 and 3.65% by mid-2028. That is a multi-hike catch-up path from a 2.29% overnight, justified only if energy pass-through becomes broad or Canada is forced to shadow the Fed.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: The seat disagrees that energy-plus-Fed-catch-up will be delivered in full through Mar-27. Headline 3% is the energy/headline print; core stays near 2%. Labor 38 and consumer 45 are slack, not 2022-style tightness. The minutes make pass-through a flagged risk, not a delivered hiking cycle. The 84bp of 2027-03 tightening is therefore an overpayment for a narrative that domestic core and labor have not validated.
context_build.price_decomposition: LEVEL: overnight 2.29% versus Mar-27 3.13% is the policy-path gap the trade owns; CA 2Y 3.27% is the sovereign echo of that catch-up, not a substitute for the CORRA path. CHANGE: CA 2Y is +31bp over 1m and -8bp on the latest day; CA 2s10s is 56bp at the 0.6th percentile of its 1y distribution, so the recent move is a bull-flattening of an already hike-priced front end rather than a new steepening. TENOR: the 2027-03 contract sits in the heart of the priced catch-up (Nov-26 1m +14bp, Dec-26 1m +29bp, Mar-27 3m +84bp) and is the locked family already held. MARGINAL DRIVER: global tightening and the energy-pass-through narrative, not a Canadian overnight move. Cross-check: CA-US 2Y -140bp and US 2Y 4.76% show the US hike is real; Canada is being asked to catch up in forwards without having moved overnight.

historical_reference.distribution: FACT: CA 2Y is at the 97.8th percentile of its 1y distribution but only the 58.5th percentile over 5y, so the stretch is versus the post-easing local history, not a 5y extreme. CA-US 2Y at -140bp is a 3.8th percentile 1y / 4.3rd percentile 5y cheap-Canada extreme. CA 2s10s at 56bp is a 0.6th percentile 1y flattening. USDCAD at the 87th percentile of 5y is the stretched FX analogue. CORRA policy path: +84bp by Mar-27 and +136bp by 2028 versus overnight 2.29%.
analogs: 2014-16 Canada energy shock: headline CPI was energy-led while Canadian policy eased as labor and core slack appeared, even as US policy and oil headlines stayed loud. Forward outcome was lower Canadian policy rates versus the energy-headline narrative.

2022-23 energy pass-through hiking cycle is the risk analog: central banks hiked through headline CPI when labor was tight and core was rising. That analog would support paying CORRA, not receiving it.
historical_reference.regime_differences: Unlike 2022, Canadian core is already near 2% and the labor gauge is 38, not a tight market. Unlike 2014-16, overnight is already 2.29% rather than the start of a fresh cutting cycle, and the CORRA curve has already prepaid 84-136bp of hikes, so the trade is fading overpriced tightening rather than forecasting a new easing cycle. The Fed has just hiked, so US-Canada decoupling is a live residual risk.

trade.thesis: FACT: CORRA overnight is 2.29% and CRAH27 implies 3.13% (+84bp), with the curve still rising toward 3.51-3.65% into 2027-28. August inflation holds at 3% with core near 2%; CA labor 38 and consumer 45. Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% and SOFR is 3.85%. INFERENCE: Mar-27 is paying 84bp of tightening for an energy-pass-through/Fed-catch-up story that domestic core and labor have not validated. A patient 2027-03 receiver earns implied-minus-realized if that path is not delivered. The same macro in spot is long USDCAD, but that pair is already an 87th-percentile 5y level with an energy-supported CAD tail, so rates is cleaner. UNKNOWN: whether pass-through lifts core enough to force the priced hikes; executable mids and CFTC positioning are absent. HOLD the locked long; do not duplicate the CORRA family.
trade.mispricing: The 84bp of tightening priced into CORRA_2027-03 (3.13% versus 2.29% overnight) overpays for a Canadian hiking cycle while overnight has not moved and underlying inflation stays near 2%. Carry is the implied-minus-realized gap, not a bet that Canada immediately eases.
why_now: The Fed hike is now realized (SOFR 3.85% on 2026-09-17) and a broader global tightening impulse (BoJ to 1.25%, hawkish BoE split) can keep leaking into CA term rates even though Canadian overnight remains 2.29%.
BoC minutes make energy pass-through a flagged risk rather than a delivered hiking cycle; core stays near 2%, so the 84bp Mar-27 gap is still a paid-to-wait receive.
Sidecar already owns long CORRA_2027-03 pos-b97bddbdbd2d at 75m; the discrepancy is intact, so the book action is HOLD rather than a duplicate OPEN or a chase ADD.
